newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: ATHLETICS - WHITEMAN TO SET PACE IN TWO-MILE RECORD ATTEMPT.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS - WHITEMAN TO SET PACE IN TWO-MILE RECORD ATTEMPT.

text.p: Briton Tony Whiteman will act as pacemaker in Saturday's two-mile clash between Ethiopian Haile Gebrselassie and Algeria's Noureddine Morceli.
The winner will pick up $1,000,000, the biggest prize in athletics history if he breaks eight minutes. Kenyan Daniel Komen holds the current world best of eight minutes 3.54 seconds.
"The organisers have asked me to go through a mile in 3:59 and to take it on to 2,000 metres in under five minutes if I can," Whiteman said.
The public pronouncements on both men's attitude to the race could not be more different.
Gebrselassie, world record holder over 5,000 metres, has said he is making this race one of the focal points of his season as he does not plan to run in the Athens world championships.

By contrast Morceli, fastest man ever over 1,500 metres, the mile and 2,000 metres, has said that he is not taking the race too seriously. The Olympic and world 1,500 metres champion has never run the distance before.
"Haile is a longer distance runner and I run middle distance," said Morceli.
"We have not had many chances to race but now we come together in the middle."
In other events on Saturday, South Africa's Olympic silver medallist Hezekiel Sepeng takes on Moroccan Mahjoub Haida of Morocco, the 1997 world indoor silver medallist.
Kim Batten of the United States, the 1995 world champion in the women's 400 metres hurdles and the holder of the world best at 52.61 seconds, runs in her specialist event.
Batten's toughest opposition should come from the current world junior champion Ulrike Urbansky of Germany.
Deon Hemmings of Jamaica, who beat Batten to take the gold in Atlanta, has decided to forsake the barriers and run over 400 metres.
